posts.post: Just started using Orion and the WinAPI-style message loop makes everything so familiar. Highly recommended for desktop apps.
You can write a fully custom control by implementing just evCreate, evPaint, evLeftButtonDown and evDestroy. The framework handles the rest through the message loop.
Use WINDOW_VSCROLL on the content window, call set_scroll_info() in evCreate, and handle evVScroll to update your pan offset. No extra child scrollbar windows needed.
RVM_ADDCOLUMN + RVM_ADDITEM to build the list, RVM_SETREDRAW(0) before bulk inserts and (1) after. Use RVM_SETREPORTCOLUMNWIDTH(0, ...) for the auto-stretch column.
Declare children in a static form_ctrl_def_t[] array, add a ctrl_binding_t[] for data exchange, then call show_dialog_from_form(). No imperative child creation needed - everything is declarative.

Yes, set UI_WINDOW_SCALE=2 in your build.

The exact same pattern applies to WINDOW_HSCROLL.
Does this work the same for WINDOW_HSCROLL?
Yes - handle evHScroll identically, just change SB_HORZ to SB_VERT.
The RVM_SETREDRAW trick alone saved me huge repaint jank - thanks!
Glad it helps - that one is documented in columnview.h.
How do you handle double-click selection?
Listen for RVN_DBLCLK in evCommand - LOWORD(wparam) is the row index.
Any way to get multi-column sorting?
Not built-in yet - you'd need to sort the data array and call feed_refresh().
The edGetText binding style for multiline edits is especially handy.
Is there a way to add validation before the dialog closes?
Yes - handle evCommand/btnClicked for ID_OK, run validation, and only call end_dialog() when it passes.
